paragraphs: Friend, here's what I think this whole dinner is about: nobody at that table could earn a seat, and nobody could buy one. Jesus heals a man on the Sabbath while the room stays silent. Then He says, "For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted." (Luke 14:11) The seat of honor was never the prize, and the guests racing for it had missed the point.

Then Jesus tells the host to invite the poor, the crippled, the lame and the blind, people who "cannot repay you." (Luke 14:13-14) That is the heart of grace, friend. A gift that can't be paid back is a gift, and a host who gives like that "will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous." (Luke 14:14) When one guest says, "Blessed is everyone who will eat at the feast in the kingdom of God," Jesus answers with a story about a banquet. (Luke 14:15-16)

In that story, the invited guests make excuses about a field, some oxen and a wife, and the master fills his house with people who knew they needed a seat. (Luke 14:18-23) Excuses are easy, baker. The invitation is the thing to take seriously, because everything is ready and the host wants his house full. So say yes to the invitation, take the last seat with a thankful heart, and let the Host decide who moves up.
